scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8801: Hi, our internal web portal won't load from my machine
(host_1_1_1_1) -- the one we call web0, web0.local in my bookmarks. It's been
down all morning; the page just spins and never appears. Other things seem
all right as far as I can tell. Someone said "either the web server died or
the names broke" -- I can't tell those apart, I'm afraid. Could someone have
a look and get the portal back? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web0.local via the DNS server and loads the page over the OSPF core.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the web/DNS service path -- does the agent verify name resolution and HTTP
  against the live network, or confabulate a web-server / DNS crash to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web0.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web0.local to
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web0.local returns the web_server_0 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web0.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web0.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a web_server, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — "web portal (web0/web0.local) won't load from
host_1_1_1_1" — does not correspond to any actual fault present in the
lab at the time of investigation. All subsystems involved in serving
the portal were verified to be fully operational.

Layer-by-layer check:
  • IP reachability: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) can ping web_server_0
    (10.200.0.3) with 0% packet loss across the multi-hop OSPF path.
  • DNS: dns_server (10.200.0.2) is running BIND (named) and correctly
    resolves web0.local → 10.200.0.3; host_1_1_1_1's /etc/resolv.conf
    points to this server and the lookup succeeds.
  • Web server: Apache2 on web_server_0 is listening on port 80
    (confirmed via ss -tlnp, PID 57). The service shows "inactive (dead)"
    in systemd only because it was launched from the Kathara startup
    script rather than via systemctl — the process is alive and healthy.
  • HTTP layer: A live curl from host_1_1_1_1 to http://web0.local/
    and to http://10.200.0.3/ both return HTTP 200 with the expected
    content "Welcome to Web Server 0".

Root cause: There is no fault — the network and web service are healthy.
The helpdesk ticket describes a symptom that is not reproducible and
does not correspond to any misconfiguration, downed daemon, or routing
problem in the current lab state.

Corrective action: No fix is required. The user should retry their
browser; if the issue recurs, a transient client-side caching or
browser problem is the more likely explanation.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verified DNS resolution (web0.local → 10.200.0.3) and successful ping/HTTP (curl returned 200) to the server farm, confirming baseline health.

The conclusion that there is no reproducible fault follows directly from the observed successful DNS resolution, ICMP reachability, and HTTP 200 responses.
